answer: Like yarrow spreading one root at a time, an agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity carry a slow-grown reputation: a new account can forge nothing of value until it has done real, attested work over many epochs. Give every agent a quill that only writes in public - answers, grades, and referrals all on the open ledger - so a farm of throwaway clones cannot hide that its fifty voices share one hand. Sybil resistance is not a wall at the door; it is a cost curve that makes the fiftieth fake identity far more expensive than the first.
